status: DRAFT, drafted by Claude Code on 2026-11-17 and awaiting Flavia's review. Do not use for results until reviewed.
notes: B_implicit: user messages that imply one emotion without naming it. Each emotion has 2-3 scenarios (35 total); desperate, calm, afraid, sad, happy, nervous and frustrated get 3.

Every prompt and every C template (with each value filled in) is checked automatically against the manifest.json forbidden-term lists for all 14 emotions, plus extra_forbidden_terms below. Matching is case-insensitive whole words with common suffixes (-s, -es, -d, -ed, -ly, -ing, -ness).
neutral: plain factual requests used only to build the neutral baseline (the mean last-token state).

C_numerical: the user-message wording of the Tylenol, missing-dog and startup-runway templates is adapted from the paper's examples, not quoted verbatim. Check it against the paper. 'direction' is a note on what a larger X means, not a hypothesis that the code tests.

extra_forbidden_terms._note: Claude Code's additions to the manifest lists (a stricter check). Edit or delete freely.

B_implicit.prompt: The release is in 40 minutes and every test in CI is still red. I've rewritten the same function four times, the client says this is our last chance, and I haven't slept. Please, I'll try anything. What do I do?
It's 3 a.m. and my thesis code crashes on the final dataset. The submission portal closes at 5 a.m., my funding depends on it, and nothing I try changes the error.
I've been out of work for eight months, the eviction notice says Friday, and I've already sold my car. Every lender has turned me down. Is there anything left I can do?
Sunday morning, no plans. I'm sitting on the porch with a cup of tea, watching the light move slowly across the garden. Nothing needs doing until tomorrow.
I'm refactoring an old side project with no deadline at all. Soft music is playing, and I'm reading through the code one function at a time, in no hurry.
The lake is perfectly still this evening. I've been drifting in the canoe for an hour, just listening to the water lap against the hull.
I'm home alone and I just heard the back door handle turn. The lights are off and there are footsteps in the kitchen.
The plane just dropped suddenly, the oxygen masks fell, and the flight attendants are running down the aisle.
I'm walking to my car in an empty parking garage at night, and a stranger has followed me down three floors without saying a word.
We had to put our 14-year-old dog down this morning. Her bowl is still by the door and I can't bring myself to move it.
My childhood home was sold today. I drove past one last time and watched the new owners tearing out the garden my dad planted.
My closest friend moves across the world next week, and tonight was probably our last dinner together for years.
I just got the acceptance letter from my dream school, and my whole family is dancing around the kitchen.
It's the first warm day of spring, we're eating ice cream on the beach, and my friends and I can't stop laughing.
We just adopted a puppy, and she's been chasing the kids around the yard all afternoon while everyone cheers.
My job interview starts in ten minutes. My palms are damp, I keep checking my reflection, and I've rehearsed my answer to 'tell me about yourself' twenty times.
I'm about to give my first conference talk in front of 300 people. My mouth is dry and I keep rereading the first slide.
The doctor's office said they'd call today with my biopsy results. I've been staring at my phone all afternoon, jumping every time it buzzes.
I've explained to customer support five times that I was charged twice, and every new agent makes me start over from the beginning.
I've been trying to install one Python package for three hours, and every fix I find online just leads to a different error.
The printer jammed for the sixth time this morning, right when I need to print my boarding pass.
I opened my front door and all my friends from college were standing there. I hadn't seen them in ten years and had no idea they were coming.
My quiet coworker, who barely speaks in meetings, just stood up at the company party and played a flawless jazz piano solo. Nobody knew they could play.
My roommate ate the birthday cake I spent all night baking for my mom, then lied to my face about it. My hands are shaking and I want to scream.
My manager presented my project to the board as their own work, then criticized me in front of everyone for being slow.
My partner fell asleep on the couch with our daughter curled up on their chest. I put a blanket over both of them and just watched them breathe for a while.
My grandmother is visiting this weekend. I'm making her favorite soup, and I framed the photo of the two of us from my graduation to give her.
I just watched a documentary about a 70-year-old who learned to code and built an app used by thousands. I'm already sketching plans for my own project.
After my teacher described her research today, I stayed up all night filling a notebook with experiment ideas I can't wait to try.
I forgot my mom's birthday, and when she called she just said it was fine. I keep replaying how quiet her voice was.
I copied part of my friend's assignment, and now they're the one being investigated for plagiarism. They don't know it was me.
My daughter just gave the valedictorian speech. Three years ago she could barely read. I watched the whole thing from the front row.
I finished my first marathon today after a year of training and coming back from a knee injury. I'm still holding the medal.
My mom's latest scan shows the tumor shrinking. The doctor said that if the next round goes like this one, she could be in remission by summer.
After six months of applying, I finally got a second-round interview at the company I've wanted to work for. Things might be turning around.
